info.title: VectorDock Capture Backend
info.description: Manual trap, QR identification, phone photo confirmation, asynchronous Modal counting, and human acceptance of candidate counts. QR identification is not authentication; SAM3 outputs are candidate detections for human review.

get.description:
Authorized trap lookup with a bounded sample slice.

sample_state filters: active (default, removed_at IS NULL),
awaiting_image (removed, no photo yet), awaiting_review (removed, has a
completed candidate, no active review), all (paginated). Defaults keep
the historical response shape.
Reload-safe, paginated image history, including unreviewed retakes.

post.description:
Check an existing call, without submitting another inference job.

The phone uses this only while a user is looking at a pending upload.
Unattended recovery remains scheduled separately. A candidate result is
not an accepted measurement and creates no measurement revision.
Audit a human choice to take a NEW photo. Never restart the old job.

ResultPreviewOut.title: ResultPreviewOut
ResultPreviewOut.description:
Read-only preview of a completed candidate result.

Exposing a candidate never creates a measurement, never sets available_at
and never accepts a sample. Retrieval of the annotation stays authorized
by the trap access grant.

ReviewStatusOut.title: ReviewStatusOut
ReviewStatusOut.description:
Review view returned by upload status.

Field semantics (documented contract):
- `state`, `measurement_id` and `measurement_revision` describe THIS
  upload's image only: they are pending_review/None while the image awaits
  human review, even when another photo of the same sample is already the
  accepted active measurement.
- `sample_active` describes the SAMPLE's active measurement (any image,
  any decision); its `revision` is the expected_measurement_revision a
  reviewer supplies to supersede it explicitly.

SampleActiveReviewOut.title: SampleActiveReviewOut
SampleActiveReviewOut.description:
The SAMPLE's active measurement (any image, any decision).

Its revision is the optimistic-concurrency token for the next explicit
replacement or correcting review (expected_measurement_revision).
